analysis: Both changed files are documentation only: changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (new) and docs/architecture/inference.md (adds a paragraph near line 252 and bumps the date). No executable source was supplied, so the actual code change is not visible. The docs describe SSD complete-checkpoint staging creating destinations "already available from host bytes" and never evaluating or fencing them, so staging does not block on MLX's process-wide evalLock; the implementing file is CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift. Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, encrypted at rest, HMAC-keyed names, salt scoping, staging reservation release paths: SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging). Items the deeper review should check in the code PR, none shown here: (1) the staged host bytes must remain only transient RAM that is authenticated (AES-GCM) before use, with no plaintext persisted or leaked; (2) skipping the eval/fence must not allow reads of unfilled or partially written destination memory, which could cause cross-request KV leakage (A-001); (3) the staging reservation accounting (GlobalKVCacheBudget) is unchanged; (4) the shorter staging time slightly changes the TTFT oracle timing under SEC-035, which is the accepted risk and is not new in kind. The claim in the changelog that a restored checkpoint never produces a first token later than cold prefill is a performance claim, not a security one. No security regression is evidenced in the supplied docs.
